summary.intent: Run the GSD docs-update workflow to generate, verify, and fix all project documentation for the cipher-box monorepo, then ship the result as a PR via the GSD ship workflow.
summary.outcome: Generated/updated 22 docs (10 canonical+gap, 12 per-package READMEs), fact-checked 17 docs against the live codebase (383+ claims), corrected all inaccuracies across 2 fix iterations, and merged a PR on branch docs/gsd-docs-update.

repo: packages/crypto/ was renamed to packages/core/ — METADATA_SCHEMAS, METADATA_EVOLUTION_PROTOCOL, and METADATA_SCHEMAS all had 15+ stale references to the old package path
apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/crypto/ directory does not exist; Rust crypto/types live in crates/core/src/ and crates/fuse/
folder.service.ts does not exist in the web app; folder depth enforcement is in apps/web/src/hooks/useFolderMutations.ts
FileMetadata and VersionEntry Rust structs are defined in crates/core/src/folder.rs — file.rs is an 11-line re-export shim; referencing file.rs for those types is wrong
TEE republish interval is 6 hours (REPUBLISH_INTERVAL_HOURS = 6), not 3 hours as documented in CAPACITY.md in 3 places
The vendored fuser source with the FUSE-T socket patch lives at apps/desktop/src-tauri/vendor/fuser/src/channel.rs, not in crates/fuse/
pnpm test:e2e and pnpm test:e2e:headed do not exist; correct scripts are test:web-e2e and test:web-e2e:headed
pnpm api:generate output is packages/api-client/, not apps/web/src/api/
There are 16 migration files in apps/api/src/migrations/, not 14; AddSignedRecordToFolderIpns and AddPublicKeyToFolderIpns were undocumented
8 load test scenario files use checkThresholds, not 5 (sdk-folder-read, sdk-ipns-contention, sdk-upload-pipeline were missed)
QUOTA_BYTES constant is defined only in crates/fuse/src/constants.rs for the FUSE layer; vault.service.ts uses only QUOTA_LIMIT_BYTES
recovery.html accepts only hex-encoded private keys (line 1102 explicitly states base64 not supported for v2); v1 inline file format is also rejected at line 931
docker-compose.yml has 5 services including someguy (delegated routing, port 8190 + libp2p 4004) which was entirely undocumented; someguy's 8190 API port is internal-only in staging
TEE worker simulator defaults to port 3001, which conflicts with mock-ipns-routing when both run locally — workaround is PORT=3002 for TEE worker
folder_ipns table has no standalone ipns_name index; indexes are IDX_folder_ipns_user_id (user_id) and UQ_folder_ipns_user_ipns (user_id, ipns_name) — owner_public_key is not a column
publicKey in the device registry is a 32-byte Ed25519 key (64 hex chars), not a 130-char uncompressed secp256k1 point

code.finding: REPUBLISH_INTERVAL_HOURS = 6, not 3 as documented in CAPACITY.md
createFolder checks parentDepth >= MAX_FOLDER_DEPTH here (not in nonexistent folder.service.ts)
moveFolder checks destDepth + 1 + subtreeDepth > MAX_FOLDER_DEPTH here
VersionEntry struct definition — file.rs is just a re-export shim
FileMetadata struct definition — file.rs is just a re-export shim
version_cooldown_ms is a u64 runtime struct field populated from VaultSettings, not a named constant VERSION_COOLDOWN_MS
publicKey validation checks length !== 64 (Ed25519 32-byte / 64 hex chars), not 130 as secp256k1 would require
TypeORM synchronize/migrations/migrationsRun config — doc had wrong line numbers 85-87
Hex-only private key input; base64 explicitly not supported for v2 recovery
v1 inline file format not supported — logs error and skips files missing fileMetaIpnsName

workflow: Background GSD doc-writer agents can hit transient API errors (socket closed, stream idle timeout) and auto-recover — the original agent may eventually complete after a respawn is already running, requiring TaskStop on the duplicate before it overwrites finished work
A process restart kills all background agents mid-flight; on restart, check actual on-disk file state before deciding whether to re-run agents
TaskStop may report agents as not-found if they died with a previous process — treat this as confirmation they are gone rather than a blocking error
markdownlint MD040 (code fence missing language tag) is enforced by lint-staged at commit time in this repo — fix fences before committing generated docs
The GSD fix loop cap is 2 iterations; after exhaustion, remaining inaccuracies with known correct values can be applied directly via Edit rather than spawning another agent
When re-verification uncovers new failures (deeper scan surfacing issues the first pass missed), these are not regressions if the originally-failing doc was already in the failing set

friction: Two Wave-1 agents (ARCHITECTURE, CONFIGURATION) hit transient API errors and had to be respawned; the originals later auto-recovered, requiring TaskStop on the duplicates to prevent file overwrites
A process restart during fix iteration 2 killed all 5 fix agents mid-flight, losing their in-process state and requiring manual edits to apply their corrections

The METADATA_SCHEMAS verifier was still running concurrently when the fix agent for the same file completed, resulting in a second post-fix report arriving late and causing confusion about iteration count

Iteration-2 fixer for METADATA_SCHEMAS used file.rs (re-export shim) for FileMetadata and VersionEntry locations instead of folder.rs where the structs are actually defined, requiring another manual correction pass
CAPACITY.md had the '5 load test scenarios' stale claim in two places (lines 299 and 337); the first fix agent only caught line 299, leaving line 337 for iteration 2
open_items: 20 VERIFY markers remain in generated docs (12 in CONFIGURATION, 6 in DEPLOYMENT, 2 in SECURITY) covering infrastructure claims not provable from the repo — e.g. Web3Auth/Google dashboard values, Grafana Cloud ingest URLs, staging host provisioning, whether GitHub private vulnerability reporting is enabled
someguy delegated-routing service (port 8190 + libp2p 4004) is now documented in DEVELOPMENT.md but the service itself has no dedicated docs explaining its role in the IPFS routing topology
TEE worker / mock-ipns-routing port-3001 collision is documented with a PORT=3002 workaround but not resolved at the configuration level

DEVELOPMENT.md informational note: the someguy service in docker-compose.yml has 2 GB memory and 1 CPU caps that may affect local development on constrained machines — worth calling out more prominently
